Coronary Stenosis Interpretation

Based on the patient's 57 model input features, the specialized machine learning models calculated the following vessel-specific probabilities:

  • Overall CAD: {CAD_RISK}% ({CAD_LABEL}) — Model-estimated likelihood of overall coronary artery disease.
  • Left Anterior Descending (LAD): {LAD_RISK}% ({LAD_LABEL}) — Anterior myocardial wall & septal perfusion
  • Left Circumflex (LCX): {LCX_RISK}% ({LCX_LABEL}) — Lateral & posterior left ventricular perfusion
  • Right Coronary Artery (RCA): {RCA_RISK}% ({RCA_LABEL}) — Inferior myocardial wall, right ventricle & nodal perfusion
Interpretation Note: Model-estimated probabilities are statistical outputs, not measured anatomical stenosis percentages, confirmed disease severity, or validated clinical diagnostic findings.

Clinical Interpretation & Next Steps

Elevated Model-Estimated Probabilities Across Multiple Vessels
Exploratory visualization criteria indicate elevated probability (≥ 50%) in multiple vessel targets. This represents an exploratory model pattern and is not a clinical diagnosis.

Educational Guidance & Scope of Use:

  • Model probabilities are statistical estimates and require qualified clinician interpretation in full medical context.
  • Actual coronary anatomy and luminal patency cannot be confirmed from machine learning probabilities alone.
  • Diagnostic testing (e.g., stress imaging or anatomical angiography) and management decisions depend on patient symptoms, physical examination, comprehensive history, and professional medical judgment.
  • This application is a research prototype and is not intended for independent clinical decision-making or prescribing therapy.

Cumulative Waterfall Decomposition: Visualizing how the patient's individual clinical features cumulatively shift model output from the baseline expected value E[f(x)] to the final model prediction f(x).
Research-Only Statistical Model Interpretation: SHAP values quantify the mathematical attribution of patient inputs to this statistical model's output on its calibrated scale (probability for Tree models, log-odds for Linear models). They reflect mathematical statistical associations within the training data distribution and do not establish biological or clinical causation. Output scale differences are preserved; log-odds contributions must not be interpreted as probability percentage changes.
57-Feature Model Input Architecture
All models evaluate the exact 57-feature vector from feature_columns.pkl structured across 7 clinical domains (Basic Demographics, Medical History, Symptoms, Vital Signs, Biomarkers, ECG Findings, Echocardiography/Physical Findings). All StandardScaler transformations are handled natively during Linear SHAP attribution.

About CardioVision AI

IIT Mandi Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026 • Track A: Cardiovascular Risk Visualization & Prediction

System Architecture & Overview

CardioVision AI is an explainable AI cardiovascular research prototype designed to bridge multimodal machine learning predictions with spatial cardiovascular visualization, combining tabular clinical biomarker inference with interactive 3D coronary anatomy.

Four-Model Machine Learning Architecture

Four independent specialized models predicting overall coronary artery disease (cad_model.pkl) and vessel-specific significant stenosis for Left Anterior Descending (lad_model.pkl), Left Circumflex (lcx_model.pkl), and Right Coronary Artery (rca_model.pkl).

57-Feature Clinical Vector Space

Seamlessly integrates 34 physiological and laboratory biomarker measurements with 23 encoded cardiac examination findings into a canonical, tamper-evident 57-dimensional patient feature vector.

Interactive Anatomical 3D Visualization

Real-time WebGL Three.js 106-mesh anatomical heart assembly with vessel-specific prediction overlays, interactive vascular territory isolation, and live telemetry overlays — not a patient-specific anatomical reconstruction.

Multimodal Pipeline & Explainability Capabilities

Medical PDF/DOCX Report Extraction & Autofill

Parses digital text reports via PyMuPDF and Word documents via python-docx (optical character recognition for scanned image-only reports requires Tesseract OCR). Identifies clinical parameters, normalizes measurement units (e.g., ft/in to cm, lbs to kg, mmol/L to mg/dL), and presents an interactive human-in-the-loop review table before autofilling the patient form with strict state invalidation.

Patient-Specific SHAP Feature Explanations

Computes local explainability attributions using TreeSHAP (LAD, LCX) and LinearSHAP (CAD, RCA). Displays top positive and negative contributing biomarkers, exact mathematical scale equivalence (probability vs. log-odds margin), and interactive cumulative waterfall breakdowns.

Prediction History & Downloadable Research PDFs

Stores patient risk evaluations in a persistent local SQLite audit database with unique snapshot hashes. Generates multi-page research evaluation PDF reports containing patient demographics, 57-feature vector tables, SHAP feature rankings, and embedded 3D coronary snapshot captures.

Standard vs. Experimental Model Modes

Provides one-click switching between baseline models (thresholds: 0.50) and candidate models (lcx_model_candidate.pkl, rca_model_candidate.pkl); uses lower classification thresholds (LCX 0.45, RCA 0.40) to enhance sensitivity for challenging circumflex and right coronary lesions.

Technology Stack

Python (Backend API & Snapshot Engine) scikit-learn (CAD, LAD, LCX & RCA Classifiers) SHAP (TreeSHAP & LinearSHAP Explanations) Three.js (WebGL 106-Mesh Anatomical Heart) HTML5 & CSS (Responsive Visual Dashboard) JavaScript (State Synchronization Engine) SQLite (Evaluation Audit History) PyMuPDF (Clinical PDF Extraction & Export) python-docx (Word Document Parsing)

Research Limitations & Validation Performance

Overall CAD ROC-AUC 0.917 High discriminative capability
LAD Stenosis ROC-AUC 0.756 Moderate-high discrimination
LCX Stenosis ROC-AUC 0.584 Limited baseline discrimination
RCA Stenosis ROC-AUC 0.652 Limited baseline discrimination
  • Retrospective Dataset: The machine learning models were evaluated on a limited retrospective single-center dataset (Z-Alizadeh Sani cohort). Model performance and generalization may differ across broader or multi-center clinical populations.
  • Limited Circumflex (LCX) and Right Coronary (RCA) Baseline Performance: Standard-mode baseline models for LCX (ROC-AUC 0.584) and RCA (ROC-AUC 0.652) exhibit limited predictive discrimination. While the Experimental Mode candidate thresholds improve sensitivity, all LCX and RCA inferences must be interpreted with heightened clinical caution.
  • Statistical Outcome Probabilities: Predictions represent statistical classification probabilities and are not clinically calibrated risk scores, direct measurements of physical arterial millimeter narrowing, or confirmed angiographic stenosis diagnoses.
  • External Clinical Validation: External prospective clinical validation in real-world clinical trials has not been established. This prototype must not be used as an independent basis for clinical diagnosis or treatment planning.
Regulatory & Research Prototype Disclaimer:

CardioVision AI is an explainable AI cardiovascular research prototype developed for the IIT Mandi Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026. It is not a certified medical device (Software as a Medical Device / SaMD) and has not been cleared or approved by any medical regulatory agency. Model-estimated probabilities, SHAP explanations, and 3D visual representations are strictly for research, educational exploration, and computer vision demonstration. They do not constitute medical advice or a substitute for professional clinical judgment, standard-of-care diagnostic coronary angiography, or cardiovascular imaging.
